Subject: SIG — details on audit event export and retention

Hi Aditya,

We're working through the SIG and have a couple of follow-ups specific to audit logging for the Redwood integration. The items we need clarified for our procurement/security review: 

- Default event retention for tenant-level event logs (how long are request/response metadata and admin events kept?)
- Supported export mechanisms: does Redwood provide an API to pull raw event streams, S3 export, or push to our SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle)?
- Can customers request a point-in-time export (for e-discovery) and what is the max time window per request?
- Evidence samples: we'd like a 24-hour sample extract with common fields (timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, event_type, user_id, model_id) for our audit team to validate schema and hashing/proof fields.
- If we request extended retention (365 days) what is the process, cost, and lead time?

Can you point to the SIG answers and attach a sample CSV or export so our team can sign off? We're aiming to close the security review by Apr 8.

Thanks —
Carlos

Subject: Re: SIG — details on audit event export and retention

Hi Carlos — thanks for the note. Below are the SIG-aligned answers and the practical steps to get you a sample export. I've attached a 24-hour redwood-log-export-sample.csv and a short evidence matrix (sig-evidence-matrix.pdf) that maps SIG questions to artifacts.

1) Retention (default):
- Tenant event logs (authentication, token issuance, admin actions, API request metadata, model download/pull events, and KMS/HSM operational events) are retained by default for 90 days.
- Inference payloads (full customer prompt/response) are not stored by default for hosted tenants unless explicitly enabled; metadata and request/response hashes are retained.

2) Extended retention (365 days):
- Available as an add-on for Dedicated and Private customers via a retention amendment.
- Lead time: typically 5–10 business days to provision storage and update retention policies; longer if we need cross-region replication.
- Pricing: we'll provide a usage-based quote (per-GB-month) — I'll ask Aditya to include the preliminary quote and DocuSign amendment once you confirm.

3) Export mechanisms supported:
- Export API: tenant-scoped REST endpoint that can return CSV/NDJSON over a secure channel (supports time-windowed exports up to 30 days per request for performance reasons).
- S3 export: scheduled delivery of daily partitioned objects to a customer-owned S3 bucket (recommended for regular ingestion into SIEMs).
- SIEM push: near-real-time forwarding to Splunk/Chronicle/QRadar via secure collector (requires initial configuration and contract add-on).

Notes on point-in-time exports / e-discovery:
- For ad-hoc e-discovery we can run a prioritized export job; we recommend splitting large ranges into 30-day windows. We provide signed checksums for each file (SHA256) and an audit manifest showing job start/end times and producer node IDs.

4) Event schema and proof fields:
- Common fields in the attached sample: timestamp_utc, tenant_id, request_id, event_type, user_id (if applicable), model_id, token_count, outcome_status, sha256_hash.
- We also emit a sequence_token and signing metadata so customers can correlate exports with live audit logs.

5) Operational steps to get your sample:
- You can choose S3 delivery (preferred) or request a one-off Export API job.
- If S3: provide a write-only role ARN + bucket path; we’ll deliver daily partitions and a 24h sample on first run.
- If Export API: we’ll run a 24-hour pull and post the CSV to a temporary secure link (expires in 7 days).

Attachments: redwood-log-export-sample.csv (sample 24h export), sig-evidence-matrix.pdf (maps SIG answers to artifacts).

Internal runbooks / tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SIG-3241
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/FS-2027-89

If you confirm preferred export method (S3 vs API) and whether you want 365d retention, I’ll open an internal provisioning ticket and provide the amendment.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
